7|a406|  Two public doors onto things every harness was already doing through private attributes.
8|3def|  
9|89fc|  **`Chat.oneshot(prompt, sp, think=, max_tokens=)`.** The stateless one-shot the cheap jobs around
10|af30|  a chat are made of - a label, a summary, a completion to insert. The public surface stopped at
11|c396|  `classify` and `structured`, so every other caller reached for `_oneshot`, and `_oneshot` took
12|4ccd|  neither a token cap nor a way to ask the model not to deliberate.
13|3def|  
14|68d7|  `think=False` is the part that matters. A cheap job's whole budget can be 32 tokens, and a
15|f270|  reasoning model will spend all of them thinking - leaving no answer to strip the thinking off of.
16|6a76|  Each backend now has a way to ask: `/no_think` in the system prompt (llama), `enable_thinking=False`
17|469a|  in the chat template (mlx), a conversation built without a thinking channel (litert), and the
18|0e64|  lowest `reasoning_effort` the API takes (remote, `NO_THINK_EFFORT`, asked again without it if the
19|5e82|  provider spells it differently). `think=True` insists wherever a backend has a switch to insist
20|af57|  with; a hosted model has none, so it keeps whatever `reasoning_effort` the chat was built with.
21|8f44|  `None` leaves the model's default alone. `classify`, `grades` and the summarizing callback ask for
22|1ce7|  `think=False` themselves now.
23|3def|  
24|d49f|  **`Chat.reconfigure(sp=, tools=)`.** Change the system prompt and the tool list on a live
25|7c64|  conversation, keeping its history - what a harness needs when a skill is discovered, a folder is
26|ae66|  opened, or an extension loads mid-session. There was no way to say it, so callers set `_sys_pre`,
27|e099|  `toolspecs` and `ns` by hand and then called `_recreate_conv`: four private names, three of which
28|325d|  only some backends have, each behind a `hasattr` because of it. Backends supply the two halves
29|e59b|  through `_set_sp` and `_set_tools`, so a backend that grows new state stays Rishi's business
30|fabe|  rather than a silent no-op in somebody else's harness.
31|3def|  
32|8829|  **`RecordCache` and `CachedChat`, and a recording CI can replay.** `RecordCache` records what an
33|506a|  expensive call returned to a diskcache directory on the first run and replays it on every run after -
34|a8c9|  `cache(key, f)`, a `key(*parts)` that hashes, and nothing else, so another package can wrap its own
35|14fb|  backend in it without inheriting any of `Chat`'s assumptions. `CachedChat` is that primitive wrapped
36|752e|  around a `Chat`. A replay builds no engine, so it costs
37|58a2|  nothing, needs no GPU, and can never start a download - which is what lets the examples in the README
38|2c9d|  actually run in CI rather than sitting behind `#| eval: false`. A miss needs `$RISHI_RECORD_CHAT`,
39|724a|  so a stale recording fails loudly instead of turning a CI job into a two-gigabyte download, and an
40|0a3c|  exception is recorded like any other reply, because a backend that rejects its own tool call is
41|133b|  exactly what the code around it has to handle.
42|3def|  
43|27fb|  The key is a `sha256` of what a reply depends on - `KEY_VERSION`, the model, the briefing, the tool
44|6688|  names, and who said what so far - and not of the bookkeeping that rides along, so a reply that gains
45|ff30|  a `usage` field or a thinking channel still replays. Once a repo commits a recording the shape of
46|b191|  that key is public API: `KEY_VERSION` is the deliberate way to break it, and it invalidates
47|2b43|  everything, everywhere, on purpose.
48|3def|  
49|3cac|  **Tag-protocol tools on hosted models.** `RemoteChat(tool_mode='tags')` puts the tool schemas
50|5b48|  in the system prompt via the new `tag_tools_sp`, sends nothing in the wire's tool field, and
51|b3a6|  reads the calls back out of the reply text. `norm_completion` now parses `<tool_call>` blocks
52|8b94|  exactly as `core.norm_resp` already did for the OpenAI-shaped path, and the stream splits them
53|f7c9|  out through `StreamSplit` so a call never renders as prose on its way to becoming a call.
54|3def|  
55|3026|  This is for a transport whose tool channel is closed rather than absent. Claude Code declares
56|49fc|  tools as an in-process MCP server, and an enterprise-managed configuration forbids every
57|da8f|  dynamic MCP server there is -- so a policy about MCP silently became a model with no tools.
58|8180|  The system prompt is the one channel no such policy can close. `tool_mode='native'` is still
59|fd76|  the default and still better wherever it works: validated schemas, structured calls back, and
60|13a4|  no dependence on the model minding its punctuation.

64|3def|  
65|99dc|  ## 0.1.1
66|1ced|  backends are split in pyproject. new ScalingWindowCallbck to autocompress. RLock and max parallel tool calls

68|f39f|  ## 0.1.0
69|3def|  
70|3a5a|  Two new backends - MLX on Apple silicon and hosted models via fastllm - plus the shared tool loop
71|5014|  and context-window management that go with them.
72|3def|  
73|46fd|  **`rishi.mlx`.** The same `Chat` API over [mlx-lm](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm), routed
74|e8ec|  automatically from an `mlx-community` model id. It is the only backend that keeps its KV cache alive
75|dd0d|  between turns: each turn is tokenized, compared against what the cache already holds, trimmed where
76|4f3b|  the two diverge, and only the new tail is prefilled - reported as `use.cached_tokens`.
77|5299|  `save_cache`/`load_cache` persist a warmed cache across sessions. Also `kv_bits` for a quantized KV
78|209c|  cache, `draft_model` for speculative decoding, and `adapter_path` for LoRA adapters.
79|3def|  
80|783e|  Vision and audio models are routed to `MlxVlmChat` (via
81|cc2d|  [mlx-vlm](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-vlm), `pip install 'rishi[mlx-vlm]'`) by reading the repo's
82|73c4|  `config.json`; `vlm=True`/`False` overrides. A text-only MLX model given an image now raises a
83|2160|  `TypeError` that names the extra to install rather than dropping the image silently.
84|3def|  
85|f8a7|  **Backends are now opt-in.** `pip install rishi` no longer pulls litert-lm-api or
86|0134|  llama-cpp-python; install what you need with `pip install 'rishi[litert]'`, `'rishi[llama]'`,
87|5b25|  `'rishi[mlx]'`, `'rishi[remote]'`, or `'rishi[all]'`. `import rishi` works with any subset installed, and `Chat(model)` imports the backend
88|20d8|  it needs on demand. Asking for a backend that isn't installed now names the extra to install.
89|3def|  
90|fde6|  **A shared tool loop.** `ToolLoopMixin` in `rishi.core` owns the Python-side tool loop for every
91|210e|  backend that receives tool calls as data (llama, MLX, remote):
92|3def|  
93|a787|  - `max_steps` is now a real budget, and is enforced on **litert** too - previously litert ignored it
94|16f6|    entirely, so a chat with tools had no cap. Past the cap, calls are denied, the model is told why,
95|2bea|    and one `final_prompt` round asks for a prose answer so the turn ends with an answer instead of a
96|71ff|    loop. Note `max_steps` now counts tool *calls* rather than tool *rounds*.
97|b736|  - `parallel_tools=True` runs independent calls from one model turn concurrently. Approval stays
98|aeaa|    sequential, so HITL prompts keep their order and the budget counts each call once; history is
99|171a|    identical either way. Not supported on litert, which runs its loop inside the engine.
100|4a76|  - A context window that fills up mid-turn is now recovered: the oldest tool results in `hist` are
101|52fe|    shrunk, backend state is rebuilt, and the model is asked to summarize. Only if that retry also
102|3de2|    fails does it raise the new `ContextWindowExceededError`.
103|3def|  
104|c723|  **llama KV-cache visibility and persistence.** llama.cpp already reuses its KV cache across turns
105|c48d|  (`Llama.generate` trims to the longest common prefix), so multi-turn chat never re-prefilled - but
106|6f74|  nothing said so, and several rishi paths silently threw the prefix away. `use.cached_tokens` now
107|686c|  reports reuse on llama as well as MLX, and is zeroed exactly when rishi invalidates the prefix: a
108|61ec|  one-shot on the shared engine (`classify`/`structured`/`check`, a shared `engine=`, a `judge=` on the
109|cda4|  same engine), a rewritten history (eviction or context recovery), or a turn carrying media. New
110|75b4|  `preserve_cache=True` saves and restores the llama state around one-shots rather than losing it, and
111|95f8|  `save_cache`/`load_cache` persist the context to disk under the same names `rishi.mlx` uses.
112|3def|  
113|a391|  **Context-window management.** `SlidingWindowCallback` keeps a long conversation from ever hitting
114|1ebe|  the wall: before each turn it checks `pct_full` and, past a threshold, drops whole message groups from
115|dcf2|  the middle of `hist` - keeping the earliest turns and the live thread - then has the backend rebuild
116|7f36|  from the shortened history. A tool call and its results are one group and are never split, and the
117|5164|  system prompt is never at risk because it lives outside `hist`. `summarize=True` replaces the dropped
118|38a1|  middle with a model-written summary. Opt in via `cbs=[SlidingWindowCallback()]`; eviction is lossy, so
119|9577|  it is not on by default. The policy is also usable directly as `evict_middle`/`msg_groups`.
120|3def|  
121|102e|  This is aimed at litert in particular, where litert-lm has no automatic KV-cache recycling
122|7368|  ([gallery#856](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/gallery/issues/856)): a full cache OOMs on GPU/NPU
123|7dcf|  and sends the CPU path into an infinite repetition loop instead of raising. `LitertChat` can now
124|9b2d|  rebuild its `Conversation` from `hist` (`_recreate_conv`), re-applying the system prompt, and if the
125|76b8|  window does fill mid-turn it evicts and retries once before raising `ContextWindowExceededError`.
126|c52d|  It previously had no context recovery at all.
127|3def|  
128|42c6|  **`rishi.remote`.** Hosted models - Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Moonshot, OpenRouter -
129|7e77|  through [fastllm](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastllm)'s `acomplete`, routed on the model name
130|9564|  (`Chat('claude-sonnet-4-5')`). It reuses `ToolLoopMixin`, so approval, the budget, parallel tools and
131|d4b8|  the callbacks behave exactly as on the local backends; the async wire call is bridged with `run_coro`
132|0a08|  and the new `sync_iter`. `tool_choice` and `reasoning_effort` are passed through natively, and
133|16a9|  provider-run tools arrive with `server=True` and are never executed locally. History converts both
134|09e2|  ways between rishi's canonical dicts and fastllm's `Msg`/`Part`, carrying images and audio as data
135|a3d1|  URLs, so a local conversation can move to a hosted model and back without losing anything.
136|3def|  
137|61d3|  **Closing fastllm gaps.** `chat(msg, stream='raw')` yields the underlying chunk dicts instead of
138|4495|  rendered markdown, for consumers that want the text/thinking/tool-call structure (`stream=True` is
139|f02c|  unchanged). `ToolCall` builds a canonical tool call as a `dict` subclass with `.name`/`.arguments`
140|c547|  accessors and a `server` flag for provider-run tools, which the loop records but never executes
141|1e53|  locally. `mk_tool_res_msg`/`mk_tool_res_msgs` are exported for driving a tool loop by hand.
142|3def|  
143|f6f9|  **Shared OpenAI-style layer.** The message, tool-schema, think/tool-tag parsing, streaming-split and
144|66fd|  usage/reminder callback helpers moved from `rishi.llama` into `rishi.core`, where MLX can share them.
145|f558|  They keep their old names in `rishi.llama`, and `rishi.llama`'s public API is unchanged.

16|c373|  all - and it sells it through a CLI rather than an API anyone else can speak. `cursor-agent` does have

22|2468|  cursor-agent -p PROMPT --output-format json --model cursor-grok-4.5-high --mode ask
23|8fc1|  {"type":"result","result":"...","session_id":"...","usage":{"inputTokens":16391,"outputTokens":30,...}}

26|d1e8|  Two consequences worth knowing before you use it.
27|3def|  
28|0e2e|  **It is not local.** The binary runs here; the model does not. `cursor-agent` is a hosted API behind a

5|1b0a|  ## Unreleased
6|3def|  
7|a406|  Two public doors onto things every harness was already doing through private attributes.
8|3def|  
9|89fc|  **`Chat.oneshot(prompt, sp, think=, max_tokens=)`.** The stateless one-shot the cheap jobs around
10|af30|  a chat are made of - a label, a summary, a completion to insert. The public surface stopped at
11|c396|  `classify` and `structured`, so every other caller reached for `_oneshot`, and `_oneshot` took
12|4ccd|  neither a token cap nor a way to ask the model not to deliberate.
13|3def|  
14|68d7|  `think=False` is the part that matters. A cheap job's whole budget can be 32 tokens, and a
15|f270|  reasoning model will spend all of them thinking - leaving no answer to strip the thinking off of.
16|6a76|  Each backend now has a way to ask: `/no_think` in the system prompt (llama), `enable_thinking=False`
17|469a|  in the chat template (mlx), a conversation built without a thinking channel (litert), and the
18|0e64|  lowest `reasoning_effort` the API takes (remote, `NO_THINK_EFFORT`, asked again without it if the
19|5e82|  provider spells it differently). `think=True` insists wherever a backend has a switch to insist
20|af57|  with; a hosted model has none, so it keeps whatever `reasoning_effort` the chat was built with.
21|8f44|  `None` leaves the model's default alone. `classify`, `grades` and the summarizing callback ask for
22|1ce7|  `think=False` themselves now.
23|3def|  
24|d49f|  **`Chat.reconfigure(sp=, tools=)`.** Change the system prompt and the tool list on a live
25|7c64|  conversation, keeping its history - what a harness needs when a skill is discovered, a folder is
26|ae66|  opened, or an extension loads mid-session. There was no way to say it, so callers set `_sys_pre`,
27|e099|  `toolspecs` and `ns` by hand and then called `_recreate_conv`: four private names, three of which
28|325d|  only some backends have, each behind a `hasattr` because of it. Backends supply the two halves
29|e59b|  through `_set_sp` and `_set_tools`, so a backend that grows new state stays Rishi's business
30|fabe|  rather than a silent no-op in somebody else's harness.
31|3def|  
32|1b32|  **`rishi.cursor`: Cursor's models through the CLI.** `CursorChat` drives `cursor-agent` headless, so
33|158a|  `Chat('cursor/cursor-grok-4.5-high')` is a chat like any other - streaming, thinking, usage, and tools
34|a779|  through the tag protocol, since the CLI hands back text and never a structured call. It cannot be a
35|4fb4|  `RemoteChat`: `cursor-agent` has an endpoint, but it is Cursor's own wire and there is nothing for
36|7d66|  fastllm to bind to.
37|3def|  
38|240a|  Two defaults are deliberate. `mode='ask'` and `sandbox='enabled'`, because `-p` on its own gives
39|39fd|  cursor-agent write and shell access to the working directory, and a second agent loose inside rishi's
40|014e|  tool loop is not what asking a model a question should mean. And `CursorChat.local` is `False`: the
41|63ed|  binary is local, the model is not, and anything deciding what is safe to send on the strength of
42|eddc|  "the runtime is not `remote`" needs to be told otherwise about this one.
43|3def|  
44|8829|  **`RecordCache` and `CachedChat`, and a recording CI can replay.** `RecordCache` records what an
45|506a|  expensive call returned to a diskcache directory on the first run and replays it on every run after -
46|a8c9|  `cache(key, f)`, a `key(*parts)` that hashes, and nothing else, so another package can wrap its own
47|14fb|  backend in it without inheriting any of `Chat`'s assumptions. `CachedChat` is that primitive wrapped
48|752e|  around a `Chat`. A replay builds no engine, so it costs
49|58a2|  nothing, needs no GPU, and can never start a download - which is what lets the examples in the README
50|2c9d|  actually run in CI rather than sitting behind `#| eval: false`. A miss needs `$RISHI_RECORD_CHAT`,
51|724a|  so a stale recording fails loudly instead of turning a CI job into a two-gigabyte download, and an
52|0a3c|  exception is recorded like any other reply, because a backend that rejects its own tool call is
53|133b|  exactly what the code around it has to handle.
54|3def|  
55|27fb|  The key is a `sha256` of what a reply depends on - `KEY_VERSION`, the model, the briefing, the tool
56|6688|  names, and who said what so far - and not of the bookkeeping that rides along, so a reply that gains
57|ff30|  a `usage` field or a thinking channel still replays. Once a repo commits a recording the shape of
58|b191|  that key is public API: `KEY_VERSION` is the deliberate way to break it, and it invalidates
59|2b43|  everything, everywhere, on purpose.
60|3def|  
61|3cac|  **Tag-protocol tools on hosted models.** `RemoteChat(tool_mode='tags')` puts the tool schemas
62|5b48|  in the system prompt via the new `tag_tools_sp`, sends nothing in the wire's tool field, and
63|b3a6|  reads the calls back out of the reply text. `norm_completion` now parses `<tool_call>` blocks
64|8b94|  exactly as `core.norm_resp` already did for the OpenAI-shaped path, and the stream splits them
65|f7c9|  out through `StreamSplit` so a call never renders as prose on its way to becoming a call.
66|3def|  
67|3026|  This is for a transport whose tool channel is closed rather than absent. Claude Code declares
68|49fc|  tools as an in-process MCP server, and an enterprise-managed configuration forbids every
69|da8f|  dynamic MCP server there is -- so a policy about MCP silently became a model with no tools.
70|8180|  The system prompt is the one channel no such policy can close. `tool_mode='native'` is still
71|fd76|  the default and still better wherever it works: validated schemas, structured calls back, and
72|13a4|  no dependence on the model minding its punctuation.

80|f39f|  ## 0.1.0
81|3def|  
82|3a5a|  Two new backends - MLX on Apple silicon and hosted models via fastllm - plus the shared tool loop
83|5014|  and context-window management that go with them.
84|3def|  
85|46fd|  **`rishi.mlx`.** The same `Chat` API over [mlx-lm](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm), routed
86|e8ec|  automatically from an `mlx-community` model id. It is the only backend that keeps its KV cache alive
87|dd0d|  between turns: each turn is tokenized, compared against what the cache already holds, trimmed where
88|4f3b|  the two diverge, and only the new tail is prefilled - reported as `use.cached_tokens`.
89|5299|  `save_cache`/`load_cache` persist a warmed cache across sessions. Also `kv_bits` for a quantized KV
90|209c|  cache, `draft_model` for speculative decoding, and `adapter_path` for LoRA adapters.
91|3def|  
92|783e|  Vision and audio models are routed to `MlxVlmChat` (via
93|cc2d|  [mlx-vlm](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-vlm), `pip install 'rishi[mlx-vlm]'`) by reading the repo's
94|73c4|  `config.json`; `vlm=True`/`False` overrides. A text-only MLX model given an image now raises a
95|2160|  `TypeError` that names the extra to install rather than dropping the image silently.
96|3def|  
97|f8a7|  **Backends are now opt-in.** `pip install rishi` no longer pulls litert-lm-api or
98|0134|  llama-cpp-python; install what you need with `pip install 'rishi[litert]'`, `'rishi[llama]'`,
99|5b25|  `'rishi[mlx]'`, `'rishi[remote]'`, or `'rishi[all]'`. `import rishi` works with any subset installed, and `Chat(model)` imports the backend
100|20d8|  it needs on demand. Asking for a backend that isn't installed now names the extra to install.
101|3def|  
102|fde6|  **A shared tool loop.** `ToolLoopMixin` in `rishi.core` owns the Python-side tool loop for every
103|210e|  backend that receives tool calls as data (llama, MLX, remote):
104|3def|  
105|a787|  - `max_steps` is now a real budget, and is enforced on **litert** too - previously litert ignored it
106|16f6|    entirely, so a chat with tools had no cap. Past the cap, calls are denied, the model is told why,
107|2bea|    and one `final_prompt` round asks for a prose answer so the turn ends with an answer instead of a
108|71ff|    loop. Note `max_steps` now counts tool *calls* rather than tool *rounds*.
109|b736|  - `parallel_tools=True` runs independent calls from one model turn concurrently. Approval stays
110|aeaa|    sequential, so HITL prompts keep their order and the budget counts each call once; history is
111|171a|    identical either way. Not supported on litert, which runs its loop inside the engine.
112|4a76|  - A context window that fills up mid-turn is now recovered: the oldest tool results in `hist` are
113|52fe|    shrunk, backend state is rebuilt, and the model is asked to summarize. Only if that retry also
114|3de2|    fails does it raise the new `ContextWindowExceededError`.
115|3def|  
116|c723|  **llama KV-cache visibility and persistence.** llama.cpp already reuses its KV cache across turns
117|c48d|  (`Llama.generate` trims to the longest common prefix), so multi-turn chat never re-prefilled - but
118|6f74|  nothing said so, and several rishi paths silently threw the prefix away. `use.cached_tokens` now
119|686c|  reports reuse on llama as well as MLX, and is zeroed exactly when rishi invalidates the prefix: a
120|61ec|  one-shot on the shared engine (`classify`/`structured`/`check`, a shared `engine=`, a `judge=` on the
121|cda4|  same engine), a rewritten history (eviction or context recovery), or a turn carrying media. New
122|75b4|  `preserve_cache=True` saves and restores the llama state around one-shots rather than losing it, and
123|95f8|  `save_cache`/`load_cache` persist the context to disk under the same names `rishi.mlx` uses.
124|3def|  
125|a391|  **Context-window management.** `SlidingWindowCallback` keeps a long conversation from ever hitting
126|1ebe|  the wall: before each turn it checks `pct_full` and, past a threshold, drops whole message groups from
127|dcf2|  the middle of `hist` - keeping the earliest turns and the live thread - then has the backend rebuild
128|7f36|  from the shortened history. A tool call and its results are one group and are never split, and the
129|5164|  system prompt is never at risk because it lives outside `hist`. `summarize=True` replaces the dropped
130|38a1|  middle with a model-written summary. Opt in via `cbs=[SlidingWindowCallback()]`; eviction is lossy, so
131|9577|  it is not on by default. The policy is also usable directly as `evict_middle`/`msg_groups`.
132|3def|  
133|102e|  This is aimed at litert in particular, where litert-lm has no automatic KV-cache recycling
134|7368|  ([gallery#856](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/gallery/issues/856)): a full cache OOMs on GPU/NPU
135|7dcf|  and sends the CPU path into an infinite repetition loop instead of raising. `LitertChat` can now
136|9b2d|  rebuild its `Conversation` from `hist` (`_recreate_conv`), re-applying the system prompt, and if the
137|76b8|  window does fill mid-turn it evicts and retries once before raising `ContextWindowExceededError`.
138|c52d|  It previously had no context recovery at all.
139|3def|  
140|42c6|  **`rishi.remote`.** Hosted models - Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Moonshot, OpenRouter -
141|7e77|  through [fastllm](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastllm)'s `acomplete`, routed on the model name
142|9564|  (`Chat('claude-sonnet-4-5')`). It reuses `ToolLoopMixin`, so approval, the budget, parallel tools and
143|d4b8|  the callbacks behave exactly as on the local backends; the async wire call is bridged with `run_coro`
144|0a08|  and the new `sync_iter`. `tool_choice` and `reasoning_effort` are passed through natively, and
145|16a9|  provider-run tools arrive with `server=True` and are never executed locally. History converts both
146|09e2|  ways between rishi's canonical dicts and fastllm's `Msg`/`Part`, carrying images and audio as data
147|a3d1|  URLs, so a local conversation can move to a hosted model and back without losing anything.
148|3def|  
149|61d3|  **Closing fastllm gaps.** `chat(msg, stream='raw')` yields the underlying chunk dicts instead of
150|4495|  rendered markdown, for consumers that want the text/thinking/tool-call structure (`stream=True` is
151|f02c|  unchanged). `ToolCall` builds a canonical tool call as a `dict` subclass with `.name`/`.arguments`
152|c547|  accessors and a `server` flag for provider-run tools, which the loop records but never executes
153|1e53|  locally. `mk_tool_res_msg`/`mk_tool_res_msgs` are exported for driving a tool loop by hand.
154|3def|  
155|f6f9|  **Shared OpenAI-style layer.** The message, tool-schema, think/tool-tag parsing, streaming-split and
156|66fd|  usage/reminder callback helpers moved from `rishi.llama` into `rishi.core`, where MLX can share them.
157|f558|  They keep their old names in `rishi.llama`, and `rishi.llama`'s public API is unchanged.

9|adf3|  A `cursor-agent` turn costs about nine seconds, and only three of them are the model. The other six

18|b038|  use it with, and the CLI otherwise. Neither group of users hits a wall.
19|3def|

22|e271|  changes underneath it - which is exactly what eviction and `reconfigure` do. So `_recreate_conv`, the

5|1b0a|  ## Unreleased
6|3def|  
7|a406|  Two public doors onto things every harness was already doing through private attributes.
8|3def|  
9|89fc|  **`Chat.oneshot(prompt, sp, think=, max_tokens=)`.** The stateless one-shot the cheap jobs around
10|af30|  a chat are made of - a label, a summary, a completion to insert. The public surface stopped at
11|c396|  `classify` and `structured`, so every other caller reached for `_oneshot`, and `_oneshot` took
12|4ccd|  neither a token cap nor a way to ask the model not to deliberate.
13|3def|  
14|68d7|  `think=False` is the part that matters. A cheap job's whole budget can be 32 tokens, and a
15|f270|  reasoning model will spend all of them thinking - leaving no answer to strip the thinking off of.
16|6a76|  Each backend now has a way to ask: `/no_think` in the system prompt (llama), `enable_thinking=False`
17|469a|  in the chat template (mlx), a conversation built without a thinking channel (litert), and the
18|0e64|  lowest `reasoning_effort` the API takes (remote, `NO_THINK_EFFORT`, asked again without it if the
19|5e82|  provider spells it differently). `think=True` insists wherever a backend has a switch to insist
20|af57|  with; a hosted model has none, so it keeps whatever `reasoning_effort` the chat was built with.
21|8f44|  `None` leaves the model's default alone. `classify`, `grades` and the summarizing callback ask for
22|1ce7|  `think=False` themselves now.
23|3def|  
24|d49f|  **`Chat.reconfigure(sp=, tools=)`.** Change the system prompt and the tool list on a live
25|7c64|  conversation, keeping its history - what a harness needs when a skill is discovered, a folder is
26|ae66|  opened, or an extension loads mid-session. There was no way to say it, so callers set `_sys_pre`,
27|e099|  `toolspecs` and `ns` by hand and then called `_recreate_conv`: four private names, three of which
28|325d|  only some backends have, each behind a `hasattr` because of it. Backends supply the two halves
29|e59b|  through `_set_sp` and `_set_tools`, so a backend that grows new state stays Rishi's business
30|fabe|  rather than a silent no-op in somebody else's harness.
31|3def|  
32|1b32|  **`rishi.cursor`: Cursor's models through the CLI.** `CursorChat` drives `cursor-agent` headless, so
33|158a|  `Chat('cursor/cursor-grok-4.5-high')` is a chat like any other - streaming, thinking, usage, and tools
34|a779|  through the tag protocol, since the CLI hands back text and never a structured call. It cannot be a
35|4fb4|  `RemoteChat`: `cursor-agent` has an endpoint, but it is Cursor's own wire and there is nothing for
36|7d66|  fastllm to bind to.
37|3def|  
38|af4e|  There are two paths to Cursor, because there are two credentials. The CLI path shells out per turn and
39|5f81|  needs only `cursor-agent login`; it costs about nine seconds a turn, of which six are the CLI starting
40|0513|  up - measured, and identical in a large repo and an empty directory, so it is init and not scanning.
41|f460|  The SDK path (`pip install 'rishi[cursor]'`, `$CURSOR_API_KEY` from the Cursor dashboard) holds one
42|d430|  `cursor_sdk` agent for the life of the chat and pays that startup once instead of once per turn.
43|d2c4|  `sdk=None` picks the SDK when there is a key and the package, and the CLI otherwise.
44|3def|  
45|cba2|  A live agent has its own memory of the conversation, so only the unsent tail goes out - the question
46|2ab9|  and any tool result, never the agent's own replies, which it already knows. That memory is a lie the
47|44d6|  moment rishi's history moves underneath it, so `_recreate_conv` - the hook eviction and `reconfigure`
48|fa52|  already call - closes the agent, and the next turn builds a fresh one and re-sends the history as it
49|372f|  now stands. Drift is not managed, it is made impossible.
50|3def|  
51|240a|  Two defaults are deliberate. `mode='ask'` and `sandbox='enabled'`, because `-p` on its own gives
52|39fd|  cursor-agent write and shell access to the working directory, and a second agent loose inside rishi's
53|014e|  tool loop is not what asking a model a question should mean. And `CursorChat.local` is `False`: the
54|63ed|  binary is local, the model is not, and anything deciding what is safe to send on the strength of
55|eddc|  "the runtime is not `remote`" needs to be told otherwise about this one.
56|3def|  
57|8829|  **`RecordCache` and `CachedChat`, and a recording CI can replay.** `RecordCache` records what an
58|506a|  expensive call returned to a diskcache directory on the first run and replays it on every run after -
59|a8c9|  `cache(key, f)`, a `key(*parts)` that hashes, and nothing else, so another package can wrap its own
60|14fb|  backend in it without inheriting any of `Chat`'s assumptions. `CachedChat` is that primitive wrapped
61|752e|  around a `Chat`. A replay builds no engine, so it costs
62|58a2|  nothing, needs no GPU, and can never start a download - which is what lets the examples in the README
63|2c9d|  actually run in CI rather than sitting behind `#| eval: false`. A miss needs `$RISHI_RECORD_CHAT`,
64|724a|  so a stale recording fails loudly instead of turning a CI job into a two-gigabyte download, and an
65|0a3c|  exception is recorded like any other reply, because a backend that rejects its own tool call is
66|133b|  exactly what the code around it has to handle.
67|3def|  
68|27fb|  The key is a `sha256` of what a reply depends on - `KEY_VERSION`, the model, the briefing, the tool
69|6688|  names, and who said what so far - and not of the bookkeeping that rides along, so a reply that gains
70|ff30|  a `usage` field or a thinking channel still replays. Once a repo commits a recording the shape of
71|b191|  that key is public API: `KEY_VERSION` is the deliberate way to break it, and it invalidates
72|2b43|  everything, everywhere, on purpose.
73|3def|  
74|3cac|  **Tag-protocol tools on hosted models.** `RemoteChat(tool_mode='tags')` puts the tool schemas
75|5b48|  in the system prompt via the new `tag_tools_sp`, sends nothing in the wire's tool field, and
76|b3a6|  reads the calls back out of the reply text. `norm_completion` now parses `<tool_call>` blocks
77|8b94|  exactly as `core.norm_resp` already did for the OpenAI-shaped path, and the stream splits them
78|f7c9|  out through `StreamSplit` so a call never renders as prose on its way to becoming a call.
79|3def|  
80|3026|  This is for a transport whose tool channel is closed rather than absent. Claude Code declares
81|49fc|  tools as an in-process MCP server, and an enterprise-managed configuration forbids every
82|da8f|  dynamic MCP server there is -- so a policy about MCP silently became a model with no tools.
83|8180|  The system prompt is the one channel no such policy can close. `tool_mode='native'` is still
84|fd76|  the default and still better wherever it works: validated schemas, structured calls back, and
85|13a4|  no dependence on the model minding its punctuation.

93|f39f|  ## 0.1.0
94|3def|  
95|3a5a|  Two new backends - MLX on Apple silicon and hosted models via fastllm - plus the shared tool loop
96|5014|  and context-window management that go with them.
97|3def|  
98|46fd|  **`rishi.mlx`.** The same `Chat` API over [mlx-lm](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx-lm), routed
99|e8ec|  automatically from an `mlx-community` model id. It is the only backend that keeps its KV cache alive
100|dd0d|  between turns: each turn is tokenized, compared against what the cache already holds, trimmed where
101|4f3b|  the two diverge, and only the new tail is prefilled - reported as `use.cached_tokens`.
102|5299|  `save_cache`/`load_cache` persist a warmed cache across sessions. Also `kv_bits` for a quantized KV
103|209c|  cache, `draft_model` for speculative decoding, and `adapter_path` for LoRA adapters.
104|3def|  
105|783e|  Vision and audio models are routed to `MlxVlmChat` (via
106|cc2d|  [mlx-vlm](https://github.com/Blaizzy/mlx-vlm), `pip install 'rishi[mlx-vlm]'`) by reading the repo's
107|73c4|  `config.json`; `vlm=True`/`False` overrides. A text-only MLX model given an image now raises a
108|2160|  `TypeError` that names the extra to install rather than dropping the image silently.
109|3def|  
110|f8a7|  **Backends are now opt-in.** `pip install rishi` no longer pulls litert-lm-api or
111|0134|  llama-cpp-python; install what you need with `pip install 'rishi[litert]'`, `'rishi[llama]'`,
112|5b25|  `'rishi[mlx]'`, `'rishi[remote]'`, or `'rishi[all]'`. `import rishi` works with any subset installed, and `Chat(model)` imports the backend
113|20d8|  it needs on demand. Asking for a backend that isn't installed now names the extra to install.
114|3def|  
115|fde6|  **A shared tool loop.** `ToolLoopMixin` in `rishi.core` owns the Python-side tool loop for every
116|210e|  backend that receives tool calls as data (llama, MLX, remote):
117|3def|  
118|a787|  - `max_steps` is now a real budget, and is enforced on **litert** too - previously litert ignored it
119|16f6|    entirely, so a chat with tools had no cap. Past the cap, calls are denied, the model is told why,
120|2bea|    and one `final_prompt` round asks for a prose answer so the turn ends with an answer instead of a
121|71ff|    loop. Note `max_steps` now counts tool *calls* rather than tool *rounds*.
122|b736|  - `parallel_tools=True` runs independent calls from one model turn concurrently. Approval stays
123|aeaa|    sequential, so HITL prompts keep their order and the budget counts each call once; history is
124|171a|    identical either way. Not supported on litert, which runs its loop inside the engine.
125|4a76|  - A context window that fills up mid-turn is now recovered: the oldest tool results in `hist` are
126|52fe|    shrunk, backend state is rebuilt, and the model is asked to summarize. Only if that retry also
127|3de2|    fails does it raise the new `ContextWindowExceededError`.
128|3def|  
129|c723|  **llama KV-cache visibility and persistence.** llama.cpp already reuses its KV cache across turns
130|c48d|  (`Llama.generate` trims to the longest common prefix), so multi-turn chat never re-prefilled - but
131|6f74|  nothing said so, and several rishi paths silently threw the prefix away. `use.cached_tokens` now
132|686c|  reports reuse on llama as well as MLX, and is zeroed exactly when rishi invalidates the prefix: a
133|61ec|  one-shot on the shared engine (`classify`/`structured`/`check`, a shared `engine=`, a `judge=` on the
134|cda4|  same engine), a rewritten history (eviction or context recovery), or a turn carrying media. New
135|75b4|  `preserve_cache=True` saves and restores the llama state around one-shots rather than losing it, and
136|95f8|  `save_cache`/`load_cache` persist the context to disk under the same names `rishi.mlx` uses.
137|3def|  
138|a391|  **Context-window management.** `SlidingWindowCallback` keeps a long conversation from ever hitting
139|1ebe|  the wall: before each turn it checks `pct_full` and, past a threshold, drops whole message groups from
140|dcf2|  the middle of `hist` - keeping the earliest turns and the live thread - then has the backend rebuild
141|7f36|  from the shortened history. A tool call and its results are one group and are never split, and the
142|5164|  system prompt is never at risk because it lives outside `hist`. `summarize=True` replaces the dropped
143|38a1|  middle with a model-written summary. Opt in via `cbs=[SlidingWindowCallback()]`; eviction is lossy, so
144|9577|  it is not on by default. The policy is also usable directly as `evict_middle`/`msg_groups`.
145|3def|  
146|102e|  This is aimed at litert in particular, where litert-lm has no automatic KV-cache recycling
147|7368|  ([gallery#856](https://github.com/google-ai-edge/gallery/issues/856)): a full cache OOMs on GPU/NPU
148|7dcf|  and sends the CPU path into an infinite repetition loop instead of raising. `LitertChat` can now
149|9b2d|  rebuild its `Conversation` from `hist` (`_recreate_conv`), re-applying the system prompt, and if the
150|76b8|  window does fill mid-turn it evicts and retries once before raising `ContextWindowExceededError`.
151|c52d|  It previously had no context recovery at all.
152|3def|  
153|42c6|  **`rishi.remote`.** Hosted models - Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek, Moonshot, OpenRouter -
154|7e77|  through [fastllm](https://github.com/AnswerDotAI/fastllm)'s `acomplete`, routed on the model name
155|9564|  (`Chat('claude-sonnet-4-5')`). It reuses `ToolLoopMixin`, so approval, the budget, parallel tools and
156|d4b8|  the callbacks behave exactly as on the local backends; the async wire call is bridged with `run_coro`
157|0a08|  and the new `sync_iter`. `tool_choice` and `reasoning_effort` are passed through natively, and
158|16a9|  provider-run tools arrive with `server=True` and are never executed locally. History converts both
159|09e2|  ways between rishi's canonical dicts and fastllm's `Msg`/`Part`, carrying images and audio as data
160|a3d1|  URLs, so a local conversation can move to a hosted model and back without losing anything.
161|3def|  
162|61d3|  **Closing fastllm gaps.** `chat(msg, stream='raw')` yields the underlying chunk dicts instead of
163|4495|  rendered markdown, for consumers that want the text/thinking/tool-call structure (`stream=True` is
164|f02c|  unchanged). `ToolCall` builds a canonical tool call as a `dict` subclass with `.name`/`.arguments`
165|c547|  accessors and a `server` flag for provider-run tools, which the loop records but never executes
166|1e53|  locally. `mk_tool_res_msg`/`mk_tool_res_msgs` are exported for driving a tool loop by hand.
167|3def|  
168|f6f9|  **Shared OpenAI-style layer.** The message, tool-schema, think/tool-tag parsing, streaming-split and
169|66fd|  usage/reminder callback helpers moved from `rishi.llama` into `rishi.core`, where MLX can share them.
170|f558|  They keep their old names in `rishi.llama`, and `rishi.llama`'s public API is unchanged.
